title: Per-entity Circuit Fabric: declarative trip policies and deterministic fallback routing
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Implement a 'Circuit Fabric' service that provides declarative, per-entity circuit breakers and deterministic fallback routing. Scope: per-tenant, per-model, and per-dependency circuits with a policy language for trip thresholds, hysteresis, and staged fallback contracts. The fabric will integrate with existing routing/mesh and the runtime so that trip decisions are made near the request path and fallbacks are executed reliably (model variant -> regional replica -> cached response -> synthetic degrade). This ticket covers the policy schema, runtime hooks, telemetry mapping to SLOs, verification harnesses, and an initial canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Policy schema that supports rate-based, latency-based, and error-rate trip rules with hysteresis and time-based annealing deployed to config service
Runtime integration so that the serving runtime consults the fabric for per-request trip decision with <5ms extra median latency for warm paths

Deterministic fallback router that can choose fallback strategy according to ordered contract (primary model variant, next-best model, regional fallback, cache, fixed-response) and records chosen path
End-to-end telemetry mapped to channel SLOs: p50/p95 latency; 1m/5m error rate; queued request depth; token-shed count and fallback-success rate
Automated chaos tests that simulate a dependency degradation and demonstrate graceful failover without violating global SLOs in staging
Console dashboard with ability to view circuit state per-entity and replay decision logs for a 24h window
Canary rollout plan executed to us-west1 with rollback criteria defined and an initial canary duration of 48h
implementation_notes: Design a compact policy DSL (YAML) that maps to runtime predicates: windowed-error-rate, latency-quantile, token-drop, and queue-length; include optional weightings for composite signals
Policy evaluation will be colocated with the routing proxy; store small per-entity state in a sharded in-memory store with async durable checkpoints
Hysteresis: implement two-phase trip state (TRIPPED -> SOFT_RECOVER -> CLOSED) with configurable cooldown and linear backoff for re-close attempts
Fallback contracts: explicit fallback tiers declared per entity. Each tier must include a cost/latency estimate and a success SL metric so routing can prefer cheaper fallbacks without exceeding SLOs
Telemetry tags: entity_id, model_hash, region, node_id, trip_reason, fallback_tier. Expose sample decision traces for audits (text logs limited to 8KB per trace).
Trade-offs considered: synchronous policy checks add micro-latency; mitigated by caching decisions for short TTLs and optimistic fast-path where policy is 'open'.
Safety: minimum-serving-path preserved — never fallback to an operation that can expose sensitive customer PII without additional RBAC checks (defer to security reviews).
test_plan: Unit tests for policy parser and evaluator; edge cases for overlapping rules and conflicting tiers
Integration tests connecting runtime -> circuit fabric -> fallback router; assertions for deterministic choice under identical inputs
Staging chaos run: throttle model replicas to trigger regional fallback and verify token-shed percentages and SLO adherence
Load test with synthetic tenants showing behavior under spike scenarios: ensure per-tenant isolation and no cross-tenant bleed
Regression harness: ensure older rollout policies remain supported and behavior is backward compatible for 90 days
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature-flagged rollout to staging; enable verbose traces for 24h and run chaos tests
Phase 1: canary in us-west1 on 5% of traffic for 48h; monitor p95 latency, error-rate, and fallback-success-rate
Phase 2: expand to us-east1 and eu-west1 with 25% traffic and observe cross-region failover metrics
Phase 3: global rollout with per-tenant opt-out for initial 2 weeks; full release if no regressions
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect trip thresholds could cause unnecessary degrading of high-value tenants. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, require tenant-level escalation to enable aggressive policies.
Risk: Policy evaluation hot-spots causing CPU pressure. Mitigation: use sampling + cached evaluations and fall back to coarse-grained global policy under overload.
Risk: Fallback contracts introducing correctness divergence across regions. Mitigation: include canary verification and cross-region consistency checks in CI
